root_cause.text: The stmmac driver's receive loop incorrectly treats unreplenished descriptors (marked 'dirty' due to allocation failure) as valid frames because it only checks the OWN flag, leading to a NULL pointer dereference when the receive cursor catches up to the dirty cursor.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explains that "stmmac_rx() only checks OWN, it confuses full/dirty" and the panic occurs "when stmmac_rx_refill() is memory-starved long enough for cur_rx to catch up to dirty_rx," while the patch introduces an explicit check `if (unlikely(next_entry == rx_q->dirty_rx)) break;` to halt processing before reaching these invalid descriptors.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix missing boundary validation in RX descriptor ring traversal to prevent processing beyond the dirty_rx marker
intent_record.what: Reordered descriptor advancement logic: first calculate next_entry using STMMAC_NEXT_ENTRY, then add a check comparing next_entry against rx_q->dirty_rx to break if they match, before finally updating rx_q->cur_rx
intent_record.how: Prevents the receive queue cursor from advancing past the dirty_rx boundary, avoiding processing of uncleaned or already-processed DMA descriptors that could cause packet corruption or data races
